name: Pix Transmissions Ltd
tagline: A niche industrial-belt exporter with a real EV two-wheeler catalyst, but the most recent quarter weakened and a trusted tracker has already exited
business_overview: Pix Transmissions manufactures rubber transmission belts (V-belts, timing belts) for industrial and, increasingly, EV two-wheeler after-market applications, with a significant export book (80+ countries) and a top-7 global position in its category.
fundamentals_table: Rs 610 Cr, Profit Rs 132 Cr; 5-yr revenue growth a weak 8.90%
fundamentals_narrative: ROCE (26.9%) is strong but ROE (7.49%) lags, and 5-year revenue growth (8.9%) has been genuinely weak -- most of the stock's ~4x move since 2020 has been P/E expansion, not sales growth, per the community's own math. The most recent quarter on record (Q4FY26, May 2026) showed sales +5% YoY but EBITDA -8% and PAT -11% YoY -- a real recent-quarter deceleration, not just a trailing-average issue.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 50 of 311 posts (Dec 2022-Aug 2026, no escalation needed). A genuine EV two-wheeler catalyst emerged in the community discussion from Jan 2025 (after-market belts for Ola/Ather EVs, priced ~Rs 3,500 each) alongside broader 2W-EV belt-drive adoption tailwinds (HDFC Securities report cited, Apr 2025). But management-transparency complaints recur throughout (no remote AGM access, sparse investor communication, no AGM notes shared for two consecutive years by mid-2025), and the most recent quarter reported (May 2026) showed a real earnings deceleration.
community_signal: akash8844 (trusted, elevated) was actively tracking, posting a bullish note in Nov 2024 (love=12) but flagging the Q4FY26 earnings weakness directly in May 2026 (love=14: 'sales up 5% YoY, but EBITDA down 8% and PAT down 11%'). Amnesiac (trusted, elevated) exited in Feb 2026 ('booked profits and moved on') after struggling to get management transparency (AGM notes).

bull_case: Genuine, real (not just narrative) EV two-wheeler after-market belt opportunity (Ola/Ather), with broader industry tailwinds toward belt-drive 2W-EVs
Strong ROCE (26.9%) and a debt-reduced balance sheet
Small-cap size (Rs 2,474 Cr) does not by itself preclude a multibagger outcome if the EV catalyst scales
bear_case: Most recent quarter (Q4FY26) showed a real deceleration -- EBITDA -8%, PAT -11% YoY -- flagged directly by a trusted tracker
5-year revenue growth (8.9%) has been genuinely weak; most of the stock's re-rating has been multiple expansion, not fundamentals, per the community's own analysis
Persistent management-transparency complaints (no remote AGM, no shared AGM notes for 2+ years) are a real governance/communication weakness
A trusted tracker has already exited specifically citing this opacity
verdict_headline: A real EV-belt catalyst exists, but the most recent quarter weakened and a trusted tracker already exited over management opacity -- not the right entry point
verdict_reasoning: The EV two-wheeler after-market opportunity is genuine, not hype, but the most recent quarter (Q4FY26) actively contradicts the growth narrative with declining EBITDA/PAT
No formal red flag, but weak recent-quarter momentum plus a trusted user's opacity-driven exit is enough negative signal to filter out this pass
Worth revisiting if a subsequent quarter shows the EV catalyst actually moving the topline, and if management communication improves

four_box.note: Verdict explicit: 'EV two-wheeler after-market opportunity is genuine, not hype' (tailwind=yes); but Q4FY26 declining EBITDA/PAT and a trusted user's opacity-driven exit undercut moat; no tam/valuation detail.
